recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is and follow up in the FHIR publisher/build tooling or routing layer so formal OperationDefinition pages render as operation definitions, show the operation name instead of Example Instance, and derive maturity/standards status from the OperationDefinition metadata.
issue_request: FHIR-26672 was a Published/Persuasive technical correction for the CodeSystem $lookup OperationDefinition. The issue began as a request to remove FMM 5, standards-status normative, and normative-version metadata from the formal OperationDefinition, but the final FHIR-I decision required the rendered formal operation page to use the operation name and match the OperationDefinition maturity and ballot status.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentions FHIR-26672. The current operation source in source/codesystem/operationdefinition-CodeSystem-lookup.xml contains FMM 5, normative-version 4.0.0, standards-status normative, and the operation title. The canonical published URL now resolves to the raw JSON OperationDefinition rather than the old R4 HTML page.
additional_context: The originating Zulip thread shows why the issue title says to remove normative claims, but FHIR-I minutes from 2020 and 2022 clarified that the formal OperationDefinition page should align labels and status with the OperationDefinition. Current build/published HTML for operation-codesystem-lookup.html still renders as Example Instance/Informative, while the raw JSON exposes FMM 5 and standards-status normative. The formal page remains referenced through the OperationDefinition examples list, and the source checkout does not include the publisher code that controls this page classification/status rendering.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. A source metadata edit would be speculative because the authoritative OperationDefinition metadata is already present and the remaining defect is in external FHIR publisher/build rendering or publication routing.
